subject: Proposal: laddered renewal with partial prepay + canary burst window
messages:
From: Maya Rudd <maya.rudd@acme.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ethan.cho@acme.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation + capacity plan for next 24 months

Jonas —

Thanks for the run-down during last week's call. As we talked about, our product team is expecting a 3x increase in peak inference concurrency through Q4 as we roll the recommendation model to 80% of users. We want to lock pricing and a capacity plan but need flexibility on how capacity is delivered: a mix of committed baseline + on-demand burst, and an option to elect multi-year pricing to secure cost predictability.

High level ask: can Redwood propose a renewal structure that:
- supports a modest committed baseline (25% of projected 3x peak) for year 1, ramping to 60% in year 2;
- includes a short "canary burst" allowance to absorb the first two months of rollout spikes without penalty;
- offers a multi-year discount if we commit 24 months up front;
- keeps an auto-renew opt-out window of 60 days before term-end.

We also need a clear true-up mechanism and a simple invoice cadence (quarterly). Maya and I will need SOW + pricing table to share with procurement and finance.

Thanks,
Maya Rudd
Head of ML Platforms, Acme AI

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Maya Rudd <maya.rudd@acme.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity plan for next 24 months

Maya —

Appreciate the details. Attaching an initial proposal and a pricing table for Acme's ramp profile. High-level response inline below and a few clarifying Qs so we can lock SOW terms.

Proposal highlights (summary):
- Year 1 baseline: commit to 25% of projected peak (we translate to token/hour and guaranteed GPU hours);
- Year 2 ramp: automatic staged uplift to 60% baseline in month 13 (with a 90-day notice window to trigger early uplift if you accelerate);
- Canary burst: first 60 days after the production rollout we provide a 150% burst allowance on top of baseline (billed at lower burst rate for the first two months), capped at X GPU-hours — we can define exact cap after you share expected spike curves;
- Multi-year: 10% discount for a 24-month committed contract (applies to baseline committed units only);
- True-up: quarterly true-up with lookback to actual peak 30-day trailing usage;
- Auto-renew: default auto-renew but a 60-day opt-out window as requested.

Questions:
1) For the canary burst, do you expect traffic spikes concentrated in a particular region? (we can localize burst capacity to reduce cross-region egress)
2) Are you open to a small upfront partial prepay (equivalent to 3 months baseline) in exchange for additional 2% discount?

Attachments: RW-Statement-of-Work-v3.pdf (pdf), pricing-table-acme-2027.xlsx (xlsx)

Will loop in Legal if you want redlines on SOW after you review.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Cho <ethan.cho@acme.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: maya.rudd@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity plan for next 24 months

Jonas / Kim —

Thanks for the proposal. Quick answers:
- Spikes will be primarily us-west (no APAC at launch) but we may short-burst east-coast for failover.
- Procurement prefers to avoid large up-front cash outlays; a 3-month partial prepay is doable if structured as a refundable credit against Q1 usage.

Two practical asks from finance/procurement:
1) Can you show the impact of the 24-month vs 12-month commitment on per-token unit cost in the pricing table?
2) We need explicit language on the canary burst billing rate and the cap so procurement can sign off.

Also tagging that Acme's security team will follow up on SOC2 evidence next week — should we expect your security questionnaire?

Cheers,
Ethan
Director, Cloud Finance — Acme AI

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Maya Rudd <maya.rudd@acme.ai>, ethan.cho@acme.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity plan for next 24 months

Ethan / Maya —

Thanks for the clarifications. Per procurement asks we've updated the pricing-table-acme-2027.xlsx with:
- side-by-side per-token unit cost for 12m vs 24m commitments;
- explicit canary burst billing: burst tokens billed at baseline rate + 20% for the first 60 days, capped at 200k GPU-hours (can reduce cap if you provide spike histogram);
- refundable credit: 3-month partial prepay placed as an invoice credit and consumed against Q1 usage (refund if unused at true-up).

On SOC2: yes, we'll send the security questionnaire and relevant artifacts to maya.security@acme.ai by Wednesday; expect the SOC2 attestation and an evidence bundle link.

Next steps:
- Maya/Ethan: confirm you can accept the 200k-hour burst cap or provide spike histogram so we can recalc;
- If yes, Jon and I will push SOW to Legal for a standard renewal amendment with multi-year pricing option + the canary clause.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Commercial Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Rudd <maya.rudd@acme.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ethan.cho@acme.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity plan for next 24 months

Kim / Jonas —

Quick update from our side: we ran a simulated rollout against a staging cluster and the 200k GPU-hour cap for the 60-day canary looks acceptable with our current spike assumptions. We'll share the spike histogram by EOD Monday so you can confirm final numbers. Finance is comfortable with the refundable 3-month credit; procurement asked for the 24-month comparison which your pricing table covered and we like the 9.5% effective discount on baseline under the multi-year commit (the 10% headline + small rounding).

Please proceed to Legal with the SOW and include the canary clause and refundable credit language. We'll aim to have procurement's signed PO within 2 weeks of receiving the redline-friendly SOW.

Thanks for moving quickly here.

Best,
Maya
